title: Rick Explains: Monolithic vs Microservices – What’s the Damn Difference?
caption: Ever wonder why some apps break when you update them? #SoftwareDevelopment

scenes.script: Alright, Morty. Picture this—one big, ugly block of code that does everything! That’s a monolithic app.
Uh, Rick… so like, if one part breaks, the whole thing breaks? That sounds awful!
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png

scenes.script: Exactly! Like your mom’s old minivan—one flat tire and the whole thing’s useless.
scenes.web_image: old minivan with a flat tire

scenes.script: But what if we split things up? Like, you know, tiny independent services that talk to each other?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png

scenes.script: Bingo! That’s microservices—each service does one thing and talks via APIs.
So, like, if one fails, the others keep working? That’s awesome!
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png
scenes.web_image: microservices architecture diagram with a broken piece

scenes.script: Exactly! It’s like a pizza delivery service—one driver crashes, but the rest keep delivering pizzas.
But why not just start with microservices then?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png

scenes.script: Good question, Morty! Monolithic is easier at first—like building a treehouse for one friend.
But when more friends show up, you need a mansion—microservices! It’s more work upfront but way better long-term.
So transitioning from monolithic to microservices is like… remodeling the treehouse into a mansion?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png

scenes.script: Yeah! And just like remodeling, you need good tools and planning. But the payoff is worth it.
